newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore moves to change election laws before poll.
newsitem.headline: Singapore moves to change election laws before poll.

text.p: Singapore is moving to raise the maximum number of members of parliament (MPs) who can be elected by multi-member constituencies ahead of general elections which must be held by April, 1997.

Two bills tabled in parliament on Tuesday by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong would allow a group representation constituency (GRC) to elect not less than three and not more than six MPs. The previous maximum was four.
Currently 60 elected parliamentary seats belong to GRCs and 21 are single-seat wards. There are four opposition members in parliament, all from single-seat constituencies.
Under the proposed changes, the actual number of MPs for each constituency would be specified by the president and there would be at least eight single-seat wards.
The changes will be debated at a later date.
According to Singapore media reports, the proposed increase is to allow for better management of town councils under the care of a group of MPs.
The latest amendments also propose the creation of new electoral divisions through the redistribution of polling districts.
